title: POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload: the spec doesn't mark the request body required, so a bodyless POST is "valid" and its 400 fails positive_data_acceptance
description:
## BLUF

`positive_data_acceptance` fails on `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload`. The pair is **not** in `schemathesis-baseline.json` at `develop` b280b74ff, so it is untriaged. It is [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks)**'s class** (positive_data_acceptance at scale), on an operation [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) doesn't name. It was raised separately, not appended, because Peter's rule is that only Backlog/Todo tickets are updated, and [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) is In Progress.

## Evidence (re-verified from source at `develop` b280b74ff, 2026-10-07)

* **Spec** (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`): `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload` has a `requestBody`, but `requestBody.required` is **unset**. Under OpenAPI an empty body is therefore spec-valid. Compare `POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate`, where `required: true`.
* **Runtime:** a request with **no body** is answered `400 {"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"Validation error","details":[{"path":["data"],"message":"Required"} …]}`.
* **Live result:** Schemathesis 4.29.4, `pre-merge`, slot 2 on Peter's Mac, stack built from the [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is) branch (no service changes), run `pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-30-16Z-slot2`, test case `P8GPsj`. Reproduce with `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer …' http://localhost:6982/api/nft/ipfs/upload`.
* **Counts are a floor:** it fired in that run and not in the run before it on the same commit.

## Fix direction

The runtime clearly requires a body (`data` is required), so declare `requestBody.required: true` in the route's OpenAPI source. Then run `npm run generate-openapi`, restart or recreate api-gateway (it serves the spec), and check whether sibling `nft` operations have the same omission.

## Done when

- [ ] The spec marks the body required, and a bodyless POST is no longer generated as a positive case.
- [ ] The pair stops firing, or is baselined against this ticket.

Found while running [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)'s pre-merge gate.

nodes.title: KS-1449: mark six nft request bodies required in the published contract

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Not run on kintsugi: needs a permitted login for a POST. Delivered: PR 1429 merged as 1fba82ddb2b8 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115 (kintsugi's REVISION head, read 2026-11-04 01:59Z). Left open.

- **Owed check:** a bodyless `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload` with a bearer refused, and the Schemathesis/Akto pair (Peter's harness).
- **Why not run:** The one permitted login attempt with the documented seed admin answered 401 at 2026-11-04 02:30Z, so by ruling it was not retried; the QA-gate owner login is permitted for single-principal GETs only and holds no admin role. The served-spec half was observed on 2026-11-03 (comment c442ff8a).

**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1429 merged as 1fba82ddb2b8 on develop (six nft request bodies marked required in the published contract), deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (carried deploy record of 2026-11-01, not re-measured today). Verified by code read and one live GET: `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/nft-certificate.openapi.ts:851` marks the mint body required, and a read-only GET of https://kintsugi.secuura.net/api/docs/openapi.json at 2026-11-03T23:13Z (200, 1,050,774 bytes, 314 paths) shows requestBody.required = true on POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload, /ipfs/pin, /ipfs/unpin, /estimate, /mint, /verify/transaction and /verify/asset (control: 132 POST operations carry a requestBody). Left open: observation owed. The 2026-10-12 comment lists as owed the Schemathesis/Akto pair run by the QA harness (it writes to its target) and a bodyless POST with a bearer; neither has been run: live sweep owed (write).

Seat J 3rd (Wednesday-briefed), verify-and-close lot L09. Measured at develop `8d34fbf0890a` on 2026-10-12; deployed means the sha that built the running image (Kintsugi anchoring, nft-certificate, transfer, originate, api-gateway: `65d7722f83a6`; timestamping, wallet-connector: `69f2045af2a4`, whose build inputs are byte-identical to `65d7722f83a6`, 0 files differ). By build record, not by a probe of the box. No state moved.

## BLUF

**Spec fixed, pinned, deployed; the done-when "the pair stops firing" is a harness result nobody has observed yet.**

* `nft-certificate.openapi.ts` marks the request body `required: true` on the ipfs upload block and on eight other blocks; `ks1364-nft-ipfs-pin-unpin-estimate-size-body-required` 6 and `ks591-nft-mint-upload-fee-body-required` 6 pass, and the full suite is 60 of 60.
* #1429 `1fba82ddb2b8` is in `65d7722f83a6`, which rebuilt nft-certificate (read only here, per the KS-535 rule).
* Owed: the Schemathesis/Akto pair run by Peter's harness (it writes to its target), and two read-only checks (the served spec, a bodyless POST with a bearer). On the sheet.
